models.name: shopping_mall_customers
models.description: Registered customer accounts with email/password credentials and authentication metadata. This is an actor table representing a true identity record in the system that owns sessions and credentials. Customers can browse products, make purchases, manage addresses, create wishlists, and write reviews. When a customer deletes their account, this record is soft-deleted but preserves all associated order history for legal compliance. The email and password_hash are required for authentication. Profile data such as name and phone are stored in separate tables.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for authentication and communication. Must be a valid email format.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for secure authentication. Never store plaintext passwords.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this customer account was created. Always recorded upon registration.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to this account. Updated whenever any field changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Null if account is active. When non-null, account is inactive but preserved for audit and order history linkage.

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_sessions
models.description:
JWT access and refresh tokens for authenticated customer sessions with expiration tracking. This table is an append-only audit trail of login events for customer actors, ensuring security compliance by capturing connection metadata (IP, referrer) and enforcing token expiration.

This table is a child of shopping_mall_customers. Each customer can have multiple sessions (1:N relationship), representing concurrent or historical logins. Sessions are never modified or deleted - only appended. They can be invalidated by system policy or customer logout, but their records remain in the database for audit.

When a customer logs in, a new session record is created. The session remains valid until either:
- The access token expires (30 minutes)
- The refresh token expires (30 days)
- The user logs out (system invalidates the refresh token)
- The admin suspends the customer account

Never use this table for storing any business data. It exists solely for authentication security and audit purposes.

@\link shopping_mall_customers.id

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer identifier this session belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: access_token
plainFields.description: JWT access token used for API authentication. Expires 30 minutes after creation.

plainFields.name: refresh_token
plainFields.description: JWT refresh token used to obtain new access tokens. Expires 30 days after creation.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address from which the login request originated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL of the page where login occurred.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led the user to the login page.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created and login occurred.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expires and becomes invalid. Always set to 30 days after created_at for refresh token.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether this session is still valid. True until token expires or is invalidated by logout/admin action.

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_password_resets

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer account requesting password reset. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Cryptographically random token issued for password reset. Must be unique and expired after use.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Absolute expiration timestamp for the reset token. Token becomes invalid after this point. Required by security policy.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset request was created. Required for audit and expiration calculation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update to record. Required temporal field for all business entities.

models.name: shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications
models.description: Email verification token record for customer account registration. Stores the unique verification token and its expiration timestamp to confirm email ownership. This subsidiary table is created during customer registration and deleted upon successful verification or expiration. Each customer can have at most one active verification record, linked to their {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer account being verified. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique verification token used to confirm email ownership during registration.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this token expires. After this time, the verification will no longer be valid and a new verification request must be made.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification record was logically deleted (e.g., after successful verification or manual cleanup). Null if still active.

models.name: shopping_mall_sellers
models.description:
Seller account records with authentication credentials and approval status. Each seller is a distinct actor with login access, independent profile management, and the ability to list products. Approval status determines whether the seller can operate on the platform.

This table stores the canonical identity record for sellers on the platform. It is referenced by sessions (shopping_mall_seller_sessions), password resets (shopping_mall_seller_password_resets), and email verifications (shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications) for authentication purposes. Profile details (name, description, logo) are managed separately in shopping_mall_seller_profiles.

A seller must be approved to list products and fulfill orders. Suspended sellers cannot log in or manage their shop. Rejected sellers cannot re-apply without admin intervention.

Relationships:
- Has many shopping_mall_seller_sessions (via seller_id)
- Has many shopping_mall_seller_password_resets (via seller_id)
- Has many shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications (via seller_id)
- Has one shopping_mall_seller_profile (via seller_id)
- Is referenced by shopping_mall_products (via seller_id)
- Is referenced by shopping_mall_order_items (via seller_id)
- Is referenced by shopping_mall_cancellation_requests (via seller_id)
- Is referenced by shopping_mall_refund_requests (via seller_id)
- Is referenced by shopping_mall_request_responses (via responder_id)
-  Is referenced by shopping_mall_admin_actions (via actor_id)

All foreign key relationships point from child tables to this actor table - never reverse direction. Never add FKs to this table pointing to other tables.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for login and communication. Must be a valid email format.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: BCrypt hash of the seller's password for authentication.

plainFields.name: approval_status
plainFields.description: Current approval status of the seller account. Valid values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected', 'suspended'. Determines account functionality: only 'approved' sellers can list products and process orders.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for rejection of seller application. Only populated when approval_status is 'rejected'. Must be provided by admin during rejection.

plainFields.name: suspended_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller account was suspended by an administrator. If null, account is not suspended. Suspended sellers cannot log in or manage their shop.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller account was registered.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller account is logically deleted. If null, account is active. This supports soft-deletion for audit purposes while preventing login.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_sessions
models.description: JWT access and refresh tokens for authenticated seller sessions with expiration tracking. This table records each successful login event for sellers, storing connection context for security auditing. Each session is tied to exactly one seller and has a fixed expiration. Sessions are managed automatically by the authentication system and are never directly modified by users.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller's account this session belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address from which the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL of the page used to initiate the session (login page).

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL from which the user navigated to the login page.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created and issued.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expires and becomes invalid. Not nullable for security.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for seller account recovery. When a seller initiates password recovery, a unique reset token is generated and stored with an expiration time. This record is destroyed upon successful reset or expiration. The token must be sufficiently random and cryptographically secure to prevent brute-force attacks, and the expiration ensures temporary access only. This table implements the password reset workflow as specified in 02-user-actors.md for sellers.

Linked to {@link shopping_mall_sellers} via seller_id. When a password reset is successful, this record is deleted. When expired, it is automatically purged by system cleanup. Never reused. Never updated after creation.

This is a session-level authentication artifact, not a business entity. It represents temporary state in the seller's authentication flow.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller account for which this password reset token was generated. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: A unique, cryptographically secure token string used for password reset. Must be generated with sufficient entropy to prevent guessing. This token is used in the reset URL sent to the seller's email. Once used or expired, this token becomes invalid.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: The exact date and time when this reset token expires. Reset requests are only valid before this timestamp. After this time, the token cannot be used and the seller must request a new password reset. Per requirements, resets must expire after a reasonable timeframe.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token was created and issued to the seller.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this token record. Never updated after creation in this domain, but included for consistency with other entities.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this token was logically deleted (used or expired). Used to maintain audit trail. If null, token is still active and not yet used.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications
models.description: Email verification tokens for seller registration. This table records the temporary verification tokens sent to new seller accounts to confirm email ownership before full activation. When a seller registers, a unique token is generated and sent to their email address. Until this token is verified (and verified_at is set), the seller account remains in a pending state and cannot access seller features. Tokens expire after a set time (e.g., 24 hours). This table is critical to ensuring that seller email addresses are valid and controlled by the registrant, preventing fraudulent registrations. Once verified, the seller may proceed with product listing and sales. This table is linked exclusively to shopping_mall_sellers and never referenced by other components. This is not a session table, but rather an authentication credential status table for the seller actor, making "actor" its correct stance.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller account that this email verification is associated with. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer account that this email verification is associated with. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: email_verification_token
plainFields.description: Unique, random, 64-character alphanumeric token generated and sent via email to confirm seller's email ownership. Token must be cryptographically secure and unguessable.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: The absolute expiration timestamp for the verification token. After this time, the token becomes invalid and must be regenerated. Always non-null to enforce security.

plainFields.name: verified_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the email verification was successfully completed by the seller. Set to non-null if email link was clicked. If NULL, verification is pending.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for when this email verification record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for last modification of this record. Updated when token is regenerated or when record is soft-deleted.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp to preserve audit trails. Null if active, non-null if canceled or expired without verification.

models.name: shopping_mall_admins
models.description: System administrator accounts with elevated privileges and email/password authentication. This table serves as the authoritative identity record for admin users, referenced by shopping_mall_admin_sessions for session management.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for administrator authentication.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for authentication. Never stored in plain text.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the admin account.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin account was logically deleted (soft delete). Nullable means account is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_sessions
models.description:
JWT access and refresh tokens for authenticated admin sessions with expiration tracking. Each record represents a single login session for an admin user and contains connection metadata including IP, referrer, and href. Sessions are append-only audit records and cannot be modified or deleted. Admin_id references the shopping_mall_admins table. All fields are required and immutable upon creation.

@link shopping_mall_admins.id

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the admin who initiated this session. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The absolute URL of the page the admin was accessing when the session was created.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The referrer URL that led the admin to the platform.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created (ISO 8601).

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires and becomes invalid (ISO 8601). Must be fixed at creation time, not updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset token records for admin account recovery. Each token is issued in response to a password reset request, contains a unique cryptographic token string, and expires after a set period. Used to validate that a requestor owns the admin account before allowing password change.

- This is a session-type table: Auxiliary to authentication flow
- Ties to one and only one admin via foreign key
- Cosigned with an admin session (when used)
- Deleted after use or expiration
- Preserved for audit trail
- Related to: {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}

All tokens are single-use. After reset, this record is marked as used and will be eventually purged by maintenance process.

plainFields.name: admin_id
plainFields.description: Reference to the admin account requesting password reset. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique hexadecimal token string used for password reset validation. Generated cryptographically random, 64 characters long.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token expires and becomes invalid. This is enforced by application logic and database-level cleanup jobs.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset request was initiated.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reset token was successfully used. Null if not yet used.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was logically deleted (soft delete). Null while active.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_actions
models.description: Immutable history of all administrative actions including approvals, rejections, suspensions, and overrides with details of actor, action type, and affected entity. This table serves as the authoritative audit trail for platform governance, ensuring every administrative intervention is permanently recorded with full context for compliance and dispute resolution. All fields are non-nullable to guarantee audit integrity and prevent tampering.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who performed this action. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of administrative action performed. Must be one of: 'approve', 'reject', 'suspend', 'ban', 'override'.

plainFields.name: affected_entity_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity this action affected. Must be one of: 'seller', 'product', 'order', 'customer', 'category'.

plainFields.name: affected_entity_id
plainFields.description: ID of the entity affected by this action (e.g., seller_id, product_id, order_id, customer_id). This references an entity in another table but cannot be foreign-keyed due to polymorphic nature; enforced by application layer.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason provided by the administrator for this action. Must be >=10 characters and <=500 characters. Enforced in application layer.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrative action was performed. Always set by system.

models.name: shopping_mall_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable store of all snapshot records for products, variants, seller profiles, reviews, and requests with complete before/after state, timestamp, actor, and versioning. Every state change in the platform (product edit, seller profile update, review modification, cancellation request) creates a continuous, unchangeable history. Used for dispute resolution, regulatory compliance, and accuracy of historical records. Records are never deleted and cannot be modified. The snapshot_data field stores a JSON object containing all fields of the entity as they existed at that precise moment, making it possible to reconstruct a product's entire history with perfect fidelity. Designed per 12-snapshot-principle.md.

Linked to core actors (customers, sellers, admins). Specialized for system-level audit trail, not business-level transactions. Referenced by shopping_mall_admin_actions, shopping_mall_cancellation_requests, shopping_mall_refund_requests, shopping_mall_seller_profile_snapshots, shopping_mall_review_snapshots to maintain integrity without duplication.

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: The actor (customer, seller, or admin) who initiated this snapshot. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id} or {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id} or {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: entity_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the target entity (product, variant, seller profile, review, request) this snapshot captures. {@link shopping_mall_products.id} or {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id} or {@link shopping_mall_seller_profiles.id} or {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id} or {@link shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.id}, etc.

foreignFields.name: preceding_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: The previous snapshot record for this same entity, if it exists, to form a version chain. {@link shopping_mall_snapshots.id}

plainFields.name: entity_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity captured (e.g., 'product', 'variant', 'seller_profile', 'review', 'cancellation_request', 'refund_request').

plainFields.name: snapshot_version
plainFields.description: Sequential version number of this snapshot for the given entity. Starts at 1 for first snapshot.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Nature of the change (e.g., 'created', 'edited', 'deleted', 'approved', 'rejected', 'canceled', 'refunded').

plainFields.name: snapshot_data
plainFields.description: JSONB field storing exact state (before and after) of the entity at time of change. Includes all fields and relationships exactly as they were. For edit: {before: {...}, after: {...}}. For delete: {before: {...}, after: {}}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Immutable timestamp when snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last time this snapshot record was updated (used for applying corrections or re-SNAshot).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Optional timestamp for logical deletion (for system cleanup or GRPA compliance). Null means active.

models.name: shopping_mall_system_settings
models.description: Global platform configuration settings that govern business rules across the entire shoppingMall ecosystem. This singleton table defines operational parameters including commission rates, subscription fees, approval timeouts, and content constraints. All values are applied system-wide and are accessible to all components. This table is managed exclusively by administrators through backend interfaces, not by end users.

plainFields.name: commission_rate
plainFields.description: Platform commission rate as a decimal percentage applied to each transaction (7.5% = 0.075).

plainFields.name: premium_subscription_fee
plainFields.description: Monthly fee for Premium Seller plan in USD (e.g., 49.00).

plainFields.name: cancellation_auto_approve_hours
plainFields.description: Number of hours after which a cancellation request is automatically approved if the seller has not responded (48 hours).

plainFields.name: refund_auto_approve_hours
plainFields.description: Number of hours after which a refund request is automatically approved if the seller has not responded (72 hours).

plainFields.name: max_product_per_seller
plainFields.description: Maximum number of products a single seller may have in their catalog (1,000).

plainFields.name: max_image_per_product
plainFields.description: Maximum number of images allowed per product listing (15).

plainFields.name: min_review_length
plainFields.description: Minimum number of characters allowed in customer review text (10).

plainFields.name: max_review_length
plainFields.description: Maximum number of characters allowed in customer review text (500).

plainFields.name: min_cancellation_reason_length
plainFields.description: Minimum number of characters required in cancellation request reason (10).

plainFields.name: max_cancellation_reason_length
plainFields.description: Maximum number of characters allowed in cancellation request reason (500).

plainFields.name: min_refund_reason_length
plainFields.description: Minimum number of characters required in refund request reason (10).

plainFields.name: max_refund_reason_length
plainFields.description: Maximum number of characters allowed in refund request reason (500).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was last updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_system_logs
models.description:
System-level logs capturing critical events such as snapshot generation failures, payment gateway errors, and platform maintenance activities. This table provides an immutable audit trail of infrastructure events to support incident response, technical troubleshooting, and compliance auditing. Every entry is generated by the system automatically; users do not interact with this table directly. This table is fundamental to system reliability and forensic analysis.

System logs should capture:
- The high-level event category (e.g., "snapshot_failure", "payment_gateway_error")
- The severity level to determine operational urgency
- Detailed contextual metadata in JSON format (e.g. error stack trace, payload, session ID)
- Precise timestamp of occurrence

These logs are append-only and permanently retained to satisfy regulatory and operational transparency requirements.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the system event occurred. Immutable and automatically captured by the system. Required for chronological ordering and audit trail.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Categorization of the system event (e.g., "snapshot_generation_failure", "payment_gateway_timeout", "maintenance_mode_enabled"). Standardized values ensure consistent filtering and reporting.

plainFields.name: severity
plainFields.description: Operational severity level of the event: 'info', 'warning', 'error', 'critical'. Used to prioritize incident response and alerting.

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: Structured JSON object containing additional context about the event. May include error stack traces, request IDs, payload snippets, server identifiers, or diagnostic information. Optional, may be null if no additional context is available.

models.name: shopping_mall_products
models.description:
Core product listings with name, description, category, and base price. Each product represents a distinct merchandise item that sellers can list for sale. Products contain the foundational information customers use to make purchasing decisions, including the product name, detailed description, category classification, and base price. All product variations (SKUs) are built on top of this core entity. Product edits trigger snapshots to preserve historical state for dispute resolution and audit purposes.

- Products are owned by sellers who register them with required metadata
- Products require a unique name and description in English
- Products are categorized under system-defined categories
- Base price must be positive and formatted with 2 decimal places
- Product images are stored separately as child entities (shopping_mall_product_images)
- Product variants are stored separately (shopping_mall_product_variants)
- Product edits create immutable snapshots via shopping_mall_snapshots mechanism
- Products can be logically deleted but never physically removed
- All properties must be preserved exactly as entered by the seller without modification

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The product name as provided by the seller. Must be unique within seller's catalog and contain 3-200 characters. Represents the title displayed to customers in search results and product listings.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the product written by the seller. Must be 10-5,000 characters long. Contains product features, specifications, usage instructions, and other information customers need to make informed decisions. Preserved exactly as submitted in product snapshots.

plainFields.name: base_price
plainFields.description: The base price of the product in the platform's currency (USD). Must be a positive number with at most two decimal places. This is the starting price before variant-specific price overrides. Used for display and calculation purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product was initially created by the seller. This is an immutable record of when the product entered the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the product. Updated whenever the product name, description, category, or base price changes. Used for determining freshness of product information.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the product was logically deleted. If null, product is active. If set, product is hidden from customer views but preserved in snapshots and audit records. Only set when seller deletes or admin suspends a product.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_images

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product that this image belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

plainFields.name: image_url
plainFields.description: The absolute URL path to the image file in storage. Must be a valid URI reference.

plainFields.name: width
plainFields.description: The width of the image in pixels. May be zero if dimensions are unknown during upload.

plainFields.name: height
plainFields.description: The height of the image in pixels. May be zero if dimensions are unknown during upload.

plainFields.name: sort_order
plainFields.description: Ordinal position for displaying this image relative to other images of the product. Must be a positive integer. 0 = first, 1 = second, etc. Required for ordered display.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this image was first uploaded. Required for audit trail and chronological order.

models.name: shopping_mall_inventory_histories
models.description:
Records every inventory change event for a product variant, including positive restocks, negative sales, and adjustment events, with reason and reference tracking.

Every inventory change (restock, sale, cancellation, refund, manual adjustment) is recorded as an immutable event. The quantity_change field uses a signed integer: positive values indicate inventory increases (restocks, refunds), negative values indicate decreases (sales, depletion). This table never stores current stock levels—those are computed by summing all history records. All changes are linked to the variant and optionally to the order, cancellation, or refund that triggered the change. This ensures complete audit trail and enables accurate stock reconciliation even after products or variants are deleted.

Reference: {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: References the specific product variant that experienced this inventory change. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.

plainFields.name: quantity_change
plainFields.description: Net change in inventory quantity. Positive for restocks, refunds, and adjustments adding stock. Negative for sales, cancellations, and adjustments removing stock. Never zero.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The business reason for the inventory change. Examples: 'order purchase', 'cancellation refund', 'refund release', 'seller adjustment', 'damaged goods', 'inventory count correction'.

plainFields.name: reference_id
plainFields.description: Optional reference to the triggering entity. Could link to shopping_mall_order_items.id (for sales), shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.id (for cancellations), or shopping_mall_refund_requests.id (for refunds). Set to null for manual adjustments.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the inventory change event. Mandatory for audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update to this record. For immutable records, this is same as created_at.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete marker. Always null for inventory history as records are permanently preserved.

models.name: shopping_mall_cart_items
models.description:
Temporary storage of product variants selected by customers before checkout. Stores the quantity of each variant chosen and preserves a snapshot of the product name, description, variant options, price, and seller profile state at the time of addition to ensure pricing and product description integrity throughout the checkout process.

All snapshot fields (product_name, product_description, variant_options, variant_price, seller_shop_name, seller_logo) are immutably captured at the moment of cart addition - meaning they reflect the exact state of the product, variant, and seller profile at the time of customer addition, not the current state. This prevents pricing fraud, product description manipulation, and seller reputation changes from affecting past checkout decisions.

Customers can add, remove, or modify quantities of items in their cart. Items are removed from cart upon successful checkout and transferred to shopping_mall_order_items with their snapshot preserved. If a seller edits their shop profile or a product is modified, the cart items remain unchanged - this is critical for the snapshot principle.

The parent entity is the customer (shopping_mall_customers). Only one cart item per variant per customer is allowed (unique index enforced).

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the product variant currently in cart. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.

plainFields.name: customer_id
plainFields.description: The customer who owns this cart item. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units of this variant in the cart. Must be >= 1.

plainFields.name: snapshot_product_name
plainFields.description: The exact product name as it existed at time of cart addition. Preserved for invoice accuracy and dispute resolution.

plainFields.name: snapshot_product_description
plainFields.description: The exact product description as it existed at time of cart addition. Preserved for invoice accuracy and dispute resolution.

plainFields.name: snapshot_variant_options
plainFields.description: JSON string containing exact variant option values at time of cart addition. Example: {"color":"blue","size":"large"}. Preserved to ensure accurate product state history.

plainFields.name: snapshot_variant_price
plainFields.description: The exact variant price (including overrides) as it existed at time of cart addition. Preserved for accurate billing, even if the current price changes.

plainFields.name: snapshot_seller_shop_name
plainFields.description: The exact shop name of the seller at time of cart addition. Preserved for accurate seller identification in order history.

plainFields.name: snapshot_seller_logo
plainFields.description: The URL pointer to the seller's logo at time of cart addition. Preserved to show exact seller branding during checkout.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cart item was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cart item was last modified (quantity updated).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cart item was logically deleted (e.g., cleared from cart or checkout completed). If null, item is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_orders
models.description:
Head record for completed customer purchases, storing order metadata including creation timestamp and shipping address at time of purchase. This table captures the immutable state of the order at time of payment confirmation, including the customer's selected shipping address and the exact order status derived from its constituent order items. Orders serve as the primary transaction record of the platform and must be preserved indefinitely for legal compliance and dispute resolution.

Relationships: 
- Belongs to one customer (via shopping_mall_customers.id)
- Contains multiple order items (via shopping_mall_order_items.order_id)
- Associated with one or more shipments (via shopping_mall_shipments.order_id)
- References snapshots of customer profile and shipping address at time of purchase (stored in shopping_mall_snapshots)

This table does NOT store individual product or variant details - those are captured in shopping_mall_order_items and their corresponding snapshots in shopping_mall_snapshots. The order head serves as a container and status manager for the complete transaction.

Key principles: 
- Immutable at creation - changes only through status transitions
- No denormalization of product/variant data - relies on child tables
- Full audit trail via global snapshot system

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who placed this order. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: order_number
plainFields.description: Unique order number in format 'ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNN' where NNNN is a sequential number within the same day.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Derived status of the entire order based on the status of its constituent items: 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', 'refunded', or 'partially completed'. This field is calculated by application logic from order_items status and should not be modified directly.

plainFields.name: total_amount
plainFields.description: Total order amount including all items, calculated as sum of order_items.item_total. Does not include shipping fees since they are not part of platform transactions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order was created upon successful payment confirmation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order status was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order was logically deleted. NULL means active. Required for soft delete pattern across all business entities.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_items
models.description: Line item record for each product variant purchased in an order, capturing the exact state of the product, variant, and seller as it existed at the time of purchase. This table serves as the immutable audit trail for all commercial transactions, preserving pricing, product details, and seller identity even if those details change later. Required for dispute resolution, financial reporting, and legal compliance. All data is frozen at checkout and never altered. References to live product/variant/seller tables are maintained only for historical context and reporting.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent order that this item belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}

foreignFields.name: variant_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the product variant that was purchased at time of purchase. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the product parent of the purchased variant at time of purchase. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller who offered this product at time of purchase. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units purchased. Must be ≥1.

plainFields.name: unit_price
plainFields.description: Exact unit price of the variant at the time of purchase, as captured in the cart snapshot. This value is immutable and should never be recalculated or updated from current pricing.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of this order item. Must be one of: 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', 'refunded'. Status changes are audited and immutable after transition.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item was created, at the moment of successful payment.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item's status was last changed.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item was logically deleted. Null means not deleted.

plainFields.name: product_name
plainFields.description: Exact product name as it appeared at time of purchase. Preserved in snapshot for audit and dispute resolution.

plainFields.name: product_description
plainFields.description: Exact product description as it appeared at time of purchase. Preserved in snapshot for audit and dispute resolution.

plainFields.name: category_id
plainFields.description: The category identifier as it existed at time of purchase. Preserved for historical categorization reporting.

plainFields.name: category_name
plainFields.description: The category name as it existed at time of purchase. Preserved for historical categorization reporting.

plainFields.name: base_price
plainFields.description: The product's base price as it existed at time of purchase. Preserved for historical pricing analysis.

plainFields.name: thumbnail_image
plainFields.description: URL of the product's thumbnail image as it existed at time of purchase. Preserved in snapshot for historical display.

plainFields.name: all_product_images
plainFields.description: JSON array of all product image URLs as they existed at time of purchase. Preserved for full historical product representation.

plainFields.name: variant_sku
plainFields.description: Exact SKU code of the purchased variant as it existed at time of purchase. Preserved for inventory reconciliation and item identification.

plainFields.name: option_values
plainFields.description: JSON object containing all option name-value pairs (e.g., {\"color\": \"red\", \"size\": \"large\"}) as they existed at time of purchase. Preserved for accurate product specification audit.

plainFields.name: variant_price
plainFields.description: The variant's price override (if any) as it existed at time of purchase. Preserved for accurate pricing audit.

plainFields.name: stock_at_time_of_purchase
plainFields.description: The variant's stock quantity at the exact moment of purchase. Preserved to verify inventory accuracy and prevent overselling disputes.

plainFields.name: shop_name
plainFields.description: Exact shop name of the seller as it existed at time of purchase. Preserved to maintain seller identity integrity in transactions.

plainFields.name: shop_description
plainFields.description: Exact shop description as it existed at time of purchase. Preserved to maintain seller reputation context and prevent manipulation.

plainFields.name: logo_url
plainFields.description: Exact seller logo URL as it existed at time of purchase. Preserved to maintain visual brand context in order history.

models.name: shopping_mall_shipments
models.description: Core shipment record containing carrier, tracking number, and delivery status for grouped order items. Each shipment corresponds to one or more order items from the same seller and represents a physical delivery event. This table is immutable after creation, with status transitions managed by system logic to ensure audit integrity. Shipment records are never deleted and must persist for 7+ years for compliance.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the order item that this shipment contains. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

plainFields.name: carrier
plainFields.description: Name of the shipping carrier (e.g., FedEx, UPS, DHL). Must be provided by seller at shipment creation. Limited to 100 characters.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Unique tracking number assigned by the carrier. Must be provided by seller. Alphanumeric, 8-32 characters. Used by customers to track shipment.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of this shipment. Must be one of: 'shipped', 'delivered', 'auto-delivered'. Starts as 'shipped' when created. Changed to 'delivered' by customer confirmation or automatically to 'auto-delivered' after 14 days.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment record was created. Used for auto-delivery triggering after 14 days.

plainFields.name: estimated_delivery_date
plainFields.description: Optional estimated delivery date provided by seller. Used for customer expectation management but does not affect system logic.

models.name: shopping_mall_cancellation_requests
models.description:
Customer-initiated cancellation requests for order items with status 'pending', including reason, requester, and auto-approval countdown. Follows 09-cancellation-refund.md specifications for 48-hour timeout.

This table captures requests made by customers to cancel order items that have been paid but not yet shipped. Each request is associated with one specific order item, contains a customer-provided reason (10-500 characters), and has an auto-approval countdown clock. If the seller doesn't respond within 48 hours, the system automatically approves the cancellation and restores inventory. This table is critical for dispute resolution between customers and sellers, preserving the exact request context at the time it was submitted.

The cancellation request is independent of the order item itself and follows a specific lifecycle: initiation → pending → auto-approved or seller-response. This separation allows for better audit trails, separate permission logic, and clear separation of concerns from order management.

The customer_id is derived through the order_item_id foreign key rather than stored directly to maintain referential integrity and avoid duplication. This design ensures that a cancellation request can only be made for an order item that the customer has previously purchased. This provides a built-in ownership validation layer.

This table has been deliberately designed as a primary entity because:
- Customers can view, initiate, and monitor cancellation requests independently
- Administrative interfaces need to list and manage all pending cancellations
- Business intelligence needs to analyze cancellation patterns across customer base
- Multiple systems (notifications, auto-approval, inventory) need to reference these requests

Following 09-cancellation-refund.md specifications: Only customers who purchased the item can request cancellation, only on 'paid' items, reason must be 10-500 characters, 48-hour auto-approval is mandatory.

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: The order item that this cancellation request pertains to. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.order_item_id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who initiated this cancellation request. This is derived from the order item, ensuring only buyers can request cancellation. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the customer for requesting cancellation. Must be between 10 and 500 characters as specified in 09-cancellation-refund.md. This field captures the customer's narrative for the request and will be displayed to the seller for response.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The current status of the cancellation request. Always 'pending' until seller responds or auto-approved by system. Values are strictly controlled by application logic per 09-cancellation-refund.md.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cancellation request was created. This is set by the system and cannot be modified by users.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cancellation request was last updated. Initially set to created_at, then updated when status changes (such as auto-approval).

plainFields.name: auto_approve_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this request will be automatically approved if no seller response occurs first. Set to created_at + 48 hours as mandated in 09-cancellation-refund.md. Used by automated job to process pending requests.

models.name: shopping_mall_refund_requests
models.description: Customer-initiated refund requests for order items with status 'delivered'. Captures refund reason, requester, and auto-approval countdown. Follows 72-hour timeout rule: if seller doesn't respond within 72 hours, system automatically approves the request. Each refund request is tied to exactly one order item and one customer. Refund requests are immutable records with status transitions and must not be edited after submission. For audit, all changes are captured in central shopping_mall_snapshots table. This table is primary mode of interaction for refund workflow.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: The order item being refunded. References the exact state of the product, variant, and price as they existed at time of purchase. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who initiated this refund request. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Textual reason provided by the customer for the refund request (minimum 10 characters, maximum 500). This is the primary field used in dispute resolution and is preserved verbatim in the immutable snapshot.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current state of the refund request. Values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'. Initial state is 'pending'. After seller response or auto-approval, it transitions to 'approved' or 'rejected'. Status changes are recorded in shopping_mall_snapshots.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the refund request was created by the customer. Must be in ISO 8601 format.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this row (e.g., when status changes). Must be in ISO 8601 format.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Used for soft deletion. If null, the request is active. If set, the request has been logically deleted (only by admin override with audit trail).

plainFields.name: auto_approval_deadline
plainFields.description: The exact timestamp when this refund request will be automatically approved if the seller has not responded. Calculated as created_at + 72 hours. Used by background job scheduler to auto-approve pending requests.

models.name: shopping_mall_request_responses
models.description:
Seller responses to cancellation or refund requests. Contains decision (approve/reject), reason for rejection (if applicable), and timestamp. Each request has exactly one response. Immutable after creation for audit trail compliance. References either a cancellation request or refund request, but never both. This table is the authoritative audit record of seller decisions in the dispute resolution process.

**Relationship**: One response exists for each cancellation or refund request (1:1). When a request is created, the response is created later by the seller. The response is immutable – once saved, the decision and reason cannot be modified. This table is referenced by the cancellation/refund request tables for status resolution and audit.

**Key Constraint**: A response must reference exactly one of the parent request tables — shopping_mall_cancellation_requests or shopping_mall_refund_requests — via mutual exclusivity enforced at application layer. Both FKs are required at the database level for referential integrity, but application logic ensures only one is populated.

**Snapshot Integration**: All changes to request status are tracked via this response record. The snapshot of the decision and reason is preserved here, not in the global shopping_mall_snapshots table, as this is a core business decision with direct financial and inventory consequences.

**Audit Role**: This table is the legal evidence of seller behavior in dispute resolution. Administrators use this table to review seller responsiveness, approval rates, and response quality.

**Referenced by**: shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.request_response_id, shopping_mall_refund_requests.request_response_id

foreignFields.name: cancellation_request_id
foreignFields.description: The cancellation request being responded to. {@link shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.id}. Exactly one of cancellation_request_id or refund_request_id must be set.

foreignFields.name: refund_request_id
foreignFields.description: The refund request being responded to. {@link shopping_mall_refund_requests.id}. Exactly one of cancellation_request_id or refund_request_id must be set.

plainFields.name: decision
plainFields.description: The seller's decision on the request. Must be exactly 'approve' or 'reject'. This is a constrained business decision with direct impact on inventory and customer experience.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the seller for rejecting the request. Must be at least 10 characters if used. Must be null if decision is 'approve'. This field is required for audit and transparency when rejection occurs.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller submitted the response. Cannot be modified after creation. Follows ISO 8601 format and is used for auto-approval timeout calculations (48h for cancellations, 72h for refunds).

models.name: shopping_mall_refund_response_snapshots
models.description: Immutable snapshots of seller refund responses. Captures exact decision and reason at time of response for audit trail.

foreignFields.name: refund_request_id
foreignFields.description: Refers to the original refund request this snapshot belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_refund_requests.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller who made this response. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: decision
plainFields.description: The seller's decision on the refund request. Must be exactly "approve" or "reject".

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the seller for the decision. Minimum 10 characters, maximum 500 characters.

plainFields.name: responded_at
plainFields.description: The exact timestamp when the seller submitted this response.

models.name: shopping_mall_reviews
models.description: Active customer reviews for products, including rating (1-5) and optional text, linked to product, order, and customer. Each review is created only after an order has been delivered. The review is considered `primary` because customers independently create, view, edit, and delete reviews across the entire platform - these are not subsidiary to any product or order. Reviews are searchable, filterable, and require full CRUD endpoints. When edited or deleted, the previous state is preserved in `shopping_mall_review_snapshots` as mandated by the snapshot principle. This table represents the current live version of the review.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: The product being reviewed. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: The order item this review is associated with. Must be unique to enforce one review per order item. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who wrote this review. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Rating given by customer, from 1 to 5. This is a required field.

plainFields.name: text
plainFields.description: Optional written feedback from the customer. Can be null if customer only provides a rating.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was originally created. Never changed.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was last edited. Null if never edited.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was logically deleted. Null if still active. Follows soft delete pattern.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_snapshots
models.description: Immutable snapshots capturing the exact state of a review at time of edit or deletion, preserving rating, text, timestamp, and actor for audit. Each snapshot represents a point-in-time copy of a review's data and cannot be modified after creation. Used for dispute resolution to verify the exact content of a review when it was viewed by other customers.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the original review that this snapshot represents. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: The customer ID who created or modified the review at the time the snapshot was taken. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: The review rating (1-5) at the time of the snapshot.

plainFields.name: text
plainFields.description: The written review text as it appeared at the time of the snapshot, or null if no text was provided.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the snapshot was created, corresponding to the time of the review edit or deletion.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the original review was last updated, which triggered this snapshot creation.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the original review was deleted, if this snapshot was created due to deletion. Otherwise null.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: The type of actor who performed the action ("customer" for reviews). This ensures auditability of review alterations.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_votes
models.description: Customer up/down votes on reviews, tracking which customer voted for which review and their vote type (helpful/not_helpful). This table enables community feedback on review quality and helps surface helpful reviews to other customers. Each vote is linked to exactly one review and one customer with a simple, normalized structure that follows the 3NF principles. Votes are ephemeral and do not require historical tracking, so no snapshot mechanism is needed. The design prevents vote manipulation by ensuring each customer can vote only once per review.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: The review being voted on. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who cast this vote. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: vote_type
plainFields.description: The type of vote cast: 'helpful' or 'not_helpful'. This is a categorical value indicating the customer's assessment of the review's usefulness.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the vote was cast. Automatically captured by the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the vote record. In this implementation, this is the same as created_at since votes are immutable after creation.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_variants
models.description: Represents specific purchasable variants of a product with unique SKU codes, option values (e.g., size, color), price overrides, and stock quantities. Each variant is owned by a seller and belongs to a single parent product. This is a primary business entity that customers can directly add to cart and purchase. All stock changes are tracked via immutable inventory_histories linked by variant_id.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: References the parent product this variant belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller who owns and manages this variant. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: sku
plainFields.description: Unique SKU code for this variant, mandatory and alphanumeric. Must be 3-20 characters. Unique constraint ensures no duplicate SKUs across all products.

plainFields.name: option_values
plainFields.description: JSONB object containing all option name-value pairs (e.g., {\"color\": \"red\", \"size\": \"large\"}) defining this variant. Stored as string for schema flexibility and searching.

plainFields.name: price_override
plainFields.description: Optional price override for this variant. If null, uses the parent product's base price. Must be zero or greater.

plainFields.name: stock
plainFields.description: Current available stock quantity for this variant. Must be zero or greater. Negative values not allowed. Increasing this triggers positive inventory_histories. Decreasing triggers negative inventory_histories.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this variant was created. Never modified.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this variant was last modified. Updated on every stock or price change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. If null, variant is active. If set, variant is logically deleted and cannot be purchased.

models.name: shopping_mall_variant_inventory_histories
models.description: Immutable audit trail recording every inventory change event for product variants. Each record represents a single quantity adjustment with reason and reference, preserving the complete history of restocks, sales, cancellations, and inventory adjustments. This table enables accurate stock level calculation and provides forensic evidence for disputes.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: The product variant this inventory change affects. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller who initiated this inventory change (if manually adjusted). May be null for system-initiated events like order fulfillment. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: The order item that triggered this inventory change (e.g., if caused by purchase, cancellation, or refund). Allows reverse lookup to order context. May be null for manual adjustments. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

plainFields.name: quantity_change
plainFields.description: The net change in stock quantity. Positive for restock/increase, negative for depletion/reduction. Always records the exact quantity changed.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The business reason for this inventory change. Examples: 'order purchase', 'cancellation refund', 'seller adjustment','system restock'. Must be human-readable and descriptive.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The exact timestamp when this inventory change was recorded in the system. Always set to the current time at commit.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp of the last update to this record. Since this is an immutable audit log, this will always equal created_at and will never be modified after creation.

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: Optional JSON field for storing additional context about the inventory change event (e.g., batch number, location, worker ID, system event ID). Must be valid JSON if provided.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_profiles
models.description: This table is a system violation. It contradicts the mandatory snapshot principle. Seller profiles must be immutable in the database. The correct source of truth for seller identity is the shopping_mall_snapshots table, which captures the exact profile state at time of every transaction. This table must be erased.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this seller profile was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this seller profile was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this profile was logically deleted. Allows for soft-deletion.

plainFields.name: shop_name
plainFields.description: Seller's shop name, visible to customers.

plainFields.name: shop_description
plainFields.description: Description of the seller's business.

plainFields.name: logo_url
plainFields.description: URL to the seller's logo image.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_profile_snapshots
models.description: Immutable historical snapshots of seller profile changes. Each record captures the complete state of a seller's shop name, description, and logo at the time of edit, ensuring accurate representation of the seller's identity as it existed at the time of any order purchase or review. This table is critical for dispute resolution and audit compliance under the mandatory snapshot principle.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller profile that this snapshot represents. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The exact shop name as it appeared at the time of the snapshot. Must be non-null to preserve state.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: The exact shop description as it appeared at the time of the snapshot. Must be non-null to preserve state.

plainFields.name: logo_url
plainFields.description: The exact logo URL as it appeared at the time of the snapshot. Must be non-null to preserve state.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when this snapshot was captured. Mandatory to track point-in-time state.
